sourceLine: your Celestial Park twin and AR work, and the questions venue teams ask before they fund a twin

cards.title: Venue Digital Twins: Validate Before Opening
cards.angle: Large enterprises hold 66.41% of the 2026 digital twin market, per Fortune Business Insights. A twin earns its cost when teams can test lighting, safety and show programming before construction ends.
cards.evidence: Your Celestial Park twin for Universal Epic Universe ran in Unreal Engine 5, with DMX control through Art-Net and sACN, so lighting could be pre-programmed on grandMA3 consoles. It measured candela, lumen and lux before the 2025 opening. Your "up to 60% faster" claim is self-reported, so confirm the basis.

cards.title: Synthetic Training Data From a Digital Twin
cards.angle: A Sept 2026 market note says twins are shifting from visualization tools to an operational backbone. Generating synthetic images for computer vision is one concrete operational use.
cards.evidence: Your Celestial Park page lists synthetic datasets for object detection, segmentation, defect detection and autonomous navigation. It frames these as covering edge cases, such as rare weather or lighting, that are impractical to capture physically.

cards.title: WebAR After 8th Wall: Plan the Migration
cards.angle: 8th Wall access ended Feb 28, 2026, and hosted content goes dark Feb 28, 2027. Teams running WebAR campaigns need a migration plan, and platform risk now belongs in the scoping conversation.
cards.evidence: Your AR Everywhere case study covers geolocated, cross-platform AR with guided narratives and branded activations. Your blog already has a WebAR versus app article, so this is a platform-risk update. Confirm what AR Everywhere runs on before claiming independence.
